thread:
maya: Leadership asked for ARR-biased RICE recalibration for Q3. Two contenders: Dedicated Pinning (enterprise retention) vs Throughput Sharding (cost). Quick take?

ria: We should add an ARR multiplier to Reach, but keep normalization so scores stay comparable.

jon: Estimates: Pinning effort 8 sprint-weeks, Reach ~12k/day, ARR concentration top-5 = 60%. Sharding effort 12 sprint-weeks, Reach ~45k/day, ARR concentration ~15%.

maya: Using ARR_mult = 1 + ARR_pct, rough calc favors Sharding on raw numbers but if normalized per-1k-req Pinning looks strong because of ARR density.

kevin: Ops needs different launch gates. Pinning gates: tenant isolation tests, per-customer rollback toggle, contract signoff. Sharding gates: throughput benchmark, cost-per-token target, cache rewarm tests. Common gate: per-route unit-econ dashboard in Console.

ria: Sequencing note: Sharding first reduces tail pressure making Pinning easier later. But sales want Pinning sooner for renewals.

maya: Proposal: run a 2-sprint spike on Sharding cost assumptions. If spike shows >20% cost improvement, prioritize Sharding; otherwise prioritize Pinning for immediate enterprise retention. Publish ARR calc and customers used.

product-bot: Reminder: last-year missing telemetry caused a bad rollout. Include that in gates (INC-2024-37).

ria: I'll draft the PRD appendix on normalizing Reach and the ARR multiplier.

maya: Thanks — will confirm action items and sync Friday. :thumbsup:
